history.content: ok this is gonna sound dumb but i found my old guitar in my parents garage last weekend lol
Not dumb at all, finding an old guitar can land in a surprisingly specific way. An old thing from a garage has a whole kind of weight to it.
ha yeah. it's all dusty and one string snapped but i kinda lit up when i saw it. i played constantly when i was like 16. badly. but constantly
"I kinda lit up" and the old, dusty guitar both stand out to me. It sounds like the guitar is carrying a lot of that 16-year-old version of you, even with one string snapped.

yeah idk. it's a good memory, my best mate and i had this 'band' that played like one party and broke up the same night lol. but holding it again was kind of a gut punch too? we don't really talk anymore
That one-night "band" and then the gut punch both matter here. What feels closest when you hold that, the good memory or the part about not really talking anymore?

honestly mostly the good part, i smile every time i think about how bad we were. but theres a little ache under it. like grateful it happened more than sad it ended? if that makes sense. (also we were SO bad. genuinely awful)
“Grateful it happened more than sad it ended” feels like the centre of it, with a little ache underneath. I’m hearing that the badness is part of what makes the memory funny and dear, too.
yeah. wistful is a good word for it. maybe ill text him a pic of the cursed guitar lol. worst case he leaves me on read which is very on brand for that band
“Wistful” fits neatly here, with a playful edge around the old band too. Does the ache feel more like missing him, or just that tender pull of the memory?
bit of both probably. but mostly just a nice pull. anyway im gonna go restring this thing and embarrass myself. thanks, this was kinda nice
A nice pull is a good way to leave it, and I hope the cursed guitar behaves itself.
